novelty.justification: The claim predicts that cross-lingual corruption "decays with typological and script distance, is asymmetric (high-resource sources contaminate more), and is causally mediated by a compact set of shared concept-binding neurons," so its novelty route is a distance-graded mechanistic account rather than merely a new multilingual setting. Searches using “cross-lingual knowledge editing interference language distance,” “multilingual counterfactual editing typological distance,” and “cross-lingual in-context knowledge editing script” identify Cross-Lingual Knowledge Editing in Large Language Models (Wang et al., ACL 2023), which already measures how source-language factual edits affect another language, and BMIKE-53 (ACL 2024), which evaluates in-context edits across 53 languages and reports script-related variation. Recasting propagation of an intentionally false edit as harmful "interference" is largely a valence change, while systematically relating its directionality to language distance and localizing it to shared neurons is a non-trivial but natural extension and integration of those established lines, not a wholly new core paradigm.
